Upgrading to the brand-new Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4? The Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 bring stronger performance and brand-new health sensing features.

However, if you don't pay attention to the differences between them, the experience in daily life is actually quite similar. From new health complications to automatic Shazam song recognition, just by adjusting a few settings, you can get the most out of your new watch. Here are some methods worth trying.

Update your watch face

First, add exclusive new complications that are only supported on the new Apple Watch models. The Series 12 and Ultra 4 can display your real-time heart rate, step count, and readiness score on the watch face.

You can add these complications to your favourite watch face, so you can gain a deeper understanding of your health and fitness status.

For me, the real-time heart rate data is an essential new complication. It only takes up one slot, and the data is more accurate than the old one which took up two slots but updated more slowly. Step tracking is also very motivating, encouraging me to start recording my activity earlier.

The readiness score will keep changing throughout the day based on your vital signs and activity level, so displaying readiness on the watch face is also a good tip.

Although it is turned off by default, you can enable the swipe-to-quickly-switch-watch-face function under "Settings > Clock > Swipe to Switch Watch Face".

Turn on automatic Shazam song recognition

Your new Apple Watch can proactively identify the music around you, without needing to call upon Siri or tap Shazam.

On your Apple Watch, go to "Settings → Smart Stack" and turn on "Music Detection". When you open the Smart Stack, the music recognition function will display the song name and the artist.

It's only a small setting change, but the next time you hear an unfamiliar song in a restaurant or a coffee shop, you will see the effect immediately.

Try the Siri Modular watch face

The Siri Modular watch face is available on all Apple Watches running watchOS 27, but the Series 12 and Ultra 4 have more complication options.

One thing I really like about the Siri Modular watch face is that its customisation style is very flexible. Right now, I'm using several Siri Modular watch faces with different colour schemes, fonts, layout styles, and complication combinations.

Give the Readiness feature some time to work

Adding the Readiness complication is only part of the setup; you also need to accumulate enough data before a score can be calculated.

Apple says you need to complete the "Health Data" setup, configure "Workout" and "Nightly Vital Signs", enable "Sleep" tracking, and wear the watch to sleep for seven consecutive nights. You also need to have sleep data from the previous night.

Find a time during the day to charge your watch, so that nighttime tracking can be maintained more easily.

For now, Readiness is an interesting experiment, but I think it is still too early to judge whether it is truly useful.

Daytime vital signs

Finally, with the hardware enhancements of the Series 12 and Ultra 4, the "Vital Signs" app offers deeper analysis.

In the "Vital Signs" app, you can see daytime data, not just nighttime data. These data are calculated based on heart rate and recovery heart rate variability. Nighttime vital signs also take into account respiratory rate and wrist temperature.

Looking ahead, the Series 12 and Ultra 4 will have more new features rolling out soon, including Siri Recap and Live Rewind.

What are your favourite ways to get the most out of your new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4? Feel free to share your insights in the comments section.
